audit.whatIsWrong: Five chart rows disagreed with the packet and with the whys[] line printed beside them: level 1 read Skill while whys[0] gives it to Gragas, levels 2-3 read Yorick while whys[1] and whys[2] call them even, levels 4-5 read Skill while whys[3] hands them to Gragas, and level 6 read Skill while whys[4] says it flips to you.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row, and every one of them already had the correct answer written in prose next to it.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet: Gragas, Skill, Skill, Gragas, Yorick, Yorick, Yorick, as matched full/content pairs with ratings rescaled.

audit.why: Level 6 is the genuine flip — Maiden plus ghouls beat Happy Hour's per-cast healing, and Explosive Cask on 100s at rank 1 cannot peel a full swarm.
audit.corrected: Kept; Barrel Roll's 10s and Body Slam's 14s rank-1 cooldowns added so the trade advice carries a number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you to wall him only after Body Slam is spent, and never mentions Drunken Rage at all.
audit.why: Dark Procession creates terrain and Body Slam collides with the first unit it charges into — the wall denies the dash outright, so it does not have to be baited first. Drunken Rage is a 5s auto-attack reset that also reduces the damage he takes, which is both the burst tell and a reason short trades into it go badly.
audit.corrected: Stated the terrain stop on the dash itself, and recorded the Drunken Rage wind-up as the step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] carries Executioner's Calling but no trading line says when the healing actually matters.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals on every skill cast, so it pays out most in the long trades the ghoul pattern forces.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds tied to extended trades in breakdown.mid.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Body Slam: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If ahead, freeze and starve him.
edits.after: Trade around Body Slam's 14s: when it is spent, run the full pattern. Happy Hour heals him off every cast, so bring Grievous Wounds to long trades.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Barrel Roll gets stronger the longer it sits, up to 4 seconds.

edits.before: Gragas edges level 1 with his Barrel Roll (Q) range and passive sustain, out-poking your Last Rites before you have ghouls, so farm safely and don't walk into barrels.
edits.after: Gragas edges level 1 with 850-range Barrel Roll and Happy Hour sustain, out-poking you before ghouls exist. His combo opens with the Drunken Rage auto reset, so the wind-up is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Through levels 2-3 it's even as your ghouls come online, but he reclaims a slight edge at 4-5 when his Q is maxed and hits hard — wall him only when his Body Slam (E) is spent so he can't slide out.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 are even as your ghouls come online, but he reclaims the edge at 4-5 with Barrel Roll maxed. Body Slam stops on the first thing it collides with, so Dark Procession denies the dash itself, not just his retreat.

edits.before: Respect his Barrel Roll (Q) poke early, but the moment he whiffs a barrel or blows Body Slam (E) to trade, wall him with Dark Procession and let ghouls collapse while his gap-close is down.
edits.after: Respect Barrel Roll early — 10s at rank 1 — and the moment he spends Body Slam to trade, cage him: it is 14s down, and Dark Procession is terrain his charge cannot cross anyway.

edits.before: Wall him after he uses Body Slam (E) so he can't escape ghouls
edits.after: Wall the lane he Body Slams through — terrain stops the dash

notes: The mirror (gragas__yorick.json) reports setting the chart to Yorick/Yorick/Yorick/Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Yorick, which conflicts with this side's packet on rows 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5.
